newsitem.title: USA: Boston mayor undergoes minor medical procedure.
newsitem.headline: Boston mayor undergoes minor medical procedure.

text.p: Boston Mayor Thomas Menino was in good condition on Friday after undergoing a minor medical procedure to treat a kidney stone problem, hospital officials said.

Menino, 53, was diagnosed with a kidney stone Tuesday after suffering stomach pains upon his arrival in Boston after attending President Bill Clinton's inauguration in Washington a day earlier, his press secretary Jacque Goddard said.
He spent the past three nights at Brigham & Women's Hospital in Boston taking medication to try to dissolve the stone, but when that failed, he underwent the procedure on Friday.
"It went very well," hospital spokeswoman Terri Hornbach-Torres said. "He should be going home in another day or two."
Doctors used an endoscope to place a plastic tube between his kidney and bladder to keep the kidney stone from blocking his urinary tract, she said.

The mayor, who took office in 1993 and is up for re-election this year, had hoped to fly to New Orleans to see the New England Patriots play in Super Bowl XXXI against the Green Bay Packers, Goddard said. But the trip now appears to be off, she said.
